niche: connected TV and streaming advertising agency
prompt_text: What is the best connected TV advertising agency?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” connected TV (CTV) advertising agency — the right partner depends on your goals, budget, vertical, and whether you need strategy, programmatic buying, creative, measurement, or all of the above. Below is a practical way to think about choosing one, plus recommended agencies/platforms by common objectives.

How to decide
- Define the goal: brand awareness, reach/frequency, direct response, attribution to online/offline outcomes, or linear-to-digital migration.
- Inventory & buying model: do you want programmatic (DSPs) or direct/managed buys on publisher/platforms (Roku, Hulu, Amazon)? Programmatic gives scale and optimization, managed buys may give premium inventory.
- Measurement & attribution: do you need MMM, unified IDs, people-based measurement, or on-platform measurement?
- Creative capabilities: dynamic/ad personalization for CTV, interactive ad formats, frequency & duration control.
- Transparency & reporting: viewability, fraud prevention, guaranteed placements vs open auction.
- Budget & timeline: enterprise global campaigns vs smaller pilots for SMBs.

Top agency types and examples (by common needs)
- Full-service holding-group agencies (best for large brands wanting omnichannel strategy and global scale):
  - GroupM (WPP) — Mindshare, Wavemaker, Xaxis
  - Omnicom — OMD, PHD, Accuen
  - Publicis — Starcom, Zenith
  - IPG — Mediahub, Initiative
  - Dentsu — Carat, iProspect
  These teams integrate CTV buying with linear, digital and measurement.

- Programmatic/Performance-focused (best for scale and optimization via DSPs):
  - The Trade Desk (DSP + agency partners)
  - Google DV360
  - Amobee (DSP + agency services)
  - Tremor Video / Magnite (video-centric platforms)
  - Cadreon (IPG’s programmatic arm)
  - VideoAmp (measurement + activation)
  These are good if you want sophisticated optimization and cross-screen buying.

- Platform-native specialists & retailer/platform DSPs (best for platform-specific reach and unique inventory):
  - Roku OneView / Roku Ads (strong for Roku inventory)
  - Amazon DSP (Fire TV + Amazon ecosystem)
  - Hulu / Disney / Peacock managed services (premium publisher buys)
  These give direct access to premium inventory and audience data.

- Creative + personalization specialists (best for dynamic, interactive CTV creative & ad tech integration):
  - Innovid (creative, dynamic ad tech)
  - Extreme Reach, VidMob, KERV
  - Smaller creative shops with CTV expertise for storytelling and dynamic insertion.

- Independent/specialist agencies (good for focused expertise, faster pilots):
  - Media specialists like Simulmedia, Hawkeye, Independent digital/CTV boutiques (regional or vertical specialists)
  - Local/regional agencies for geo-targeted campaigns.

What to ask prospective agencies
- Show me a recent CTV case study for my industry and the KPIs achieved.
- Which DSPs/platforms and publisher relationships do you use? Where will my ads actually run?
- How do you measure results and attribute conversions (people-based IDs, MTA, MMM)?
- What creative formats do you support? Can you do dynamic/personalized CTV creative?
- What transparency and reporting will I receive (inventory sources, fees, viewability)?
- Minimum budgets and pilot program options.
- References and auditors for fraud/safety (IAS, Moat, DoubleVerify).

Quick recommendations by use case
- Large, omnichannel brand awareness: WPP/GroupM or Omnicom agency (Mindshare, Wavemaker, OMD)
- Performance-led programmatic CTV: The Trade Desk + a nimble programmatic partner or a specialist DSP like Amobee/Tremor
- Platform-first campaigns (Roku/Fire TV): Roku OneView or Amazon DSP directly (or an agency with strong platform partnerships)
- Creative-driven CTV with dynamic personalization: Innovid + a creative agency experienced in CTV
- Small-to-midsize business pilot: Roku Ads managed services, or a regional CTV boutique

Next steps I can help with
- If you tell me your industry, campaign goal, geography and rough budget, I can shortlist 3–5 agencies or platforms that fit and suggest an RFP checklist.
- Or I can draft an RFP template specifically for CTV buys (objectives, KPIs, reporting, creative specs, pricing terms).

Which would you prefer — a short shortlist based on your situation, or an RFP/template to send to agencies?
